parts.text:

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Explain why the lattice energy, $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}$, of ZnO is more exothermic than that of ZnS.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Zinc metal can be obtained in a two-step process as shown.

step 1 $2\text{ZnS(s)} + 3\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{ZnO(s)} + 2\text{SO}_2\text{(g)}$

step 2 $\text{ZnO(s)} + \text{C(s)} \rightarrow \text{Zn(l)} + \text{CO(g)}$

The reactions are carried out at $800^{\circ}\text{C}$.
parts.text:
Predict the sign of the entropy change, $\Delta S^{\ominus}$, of the reaction in **step 1**.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the data in Table 1.1 to calculate $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ of the reaction shown in **step 2**.

Table 1.1

| chemical | $\text{ZnO(s)}$ | $\text{C(s)}$ | $\text{Zn(l)}$ | $\text{CO(g)}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $S^{\ominus} / \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ | 43.7 | 5.7 | 50.8 | 197.7 |

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
An equation for the direct reduction of ZnS by carbon is shown.

$$2\text{ZnS(s)} + \text{C(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{Zn(l)} + \text{CS}_2\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H^{\ominus} = +733\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta S^{\ominus} = +218\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$$

This reaction is **not** feasible at $800^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Calculate $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ for this reaction at $800^{\circ}\text{C}$.
